newsitem.title: UK: Dollar dips in Europe as mark gains on crosses.
newsitem.headline: Dollar dips in Europe as mark gains on crosses.

text.p: LONDON, May 28 Reuter) - The dollar was weaker against the mark in late Europe, pressured by mark strength against its European satellites.
Nerves over the forthcoming final round of French elections and the growing prospect of an opposition Socialist win sent mark/French franc to near four-month highs above 3.38 francs.

"The interpretation of the French election was a soft euro and soft mark but the market view is that has been overdone," said Claudio Demolli, foreign exchange analyst at Merrill Lynch in London. "The old pattern of trouble in Europe helping the mark is reemerging."
By 1535 GMT the dollar was trading at 1.6920/30 marks, down from an overnight high of 1.7071 marks and late Tuesday's European level of 1.7045/50 marks.
Against the yen, the dollar was also weaker at 115.44/54, well below its overnight high of 117.00 and down from 116.51/65 yen late Tuesday.

The dollar took little notice of a rise in U.S. April durable goods data slightly above expectations. April orders rose a headline 1.4 percent against a 1.3 percent rise forecast and a revised 2.2 percent drop in March. However, without transportation orders, April orders were only up 0.5 percent.
Dollar/mark was hit earlier by rumours that Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer was set to resign, later denied by the Bundesbank.
"The resignation rumours were clearly nonsense, but logic seems to have gone out of the window for the time being," said Julian Jessop, European economist at Nikko Europe.

The rumours and denial come before a Bundesbank statement at 1700 GMT on Germany's reserves revaluation plans. Bundesbank member Hans-Juergen Koebnick said the statement would be "worth reading and brief". Koebnick said the statement would contain no surprises, "although some may be surprised at it," he added.
The dollar remained relatively steady against the Swiss franc, pressured by the weaker dollar/mark but finding support in the Swiss National Bank's efforts to offset recent Swiss franc strength.
The Swiss central bank continued to add liquidity to the money market, adding short-dated funds at one percent for the second day in a row earlier today.
Dollar/Swiss franc was trading at 1.4155/65 francs, off earlier highs of 1.4260 marks and just below late Tuesday's 1.4192/97 francs.
